name: Voodoo Child
reference: Voodoo Child (Slight Return) (88 BPM, Eb): The Jimi Hendrix Experience, Electric Ladyland (1968; May 3 1968, Record Plant NYC, eng. Eddie Kramer, prod. Chas Chandler)
rig: Fender Stratocaster (tuned down a half step) -> wah (intro; model undocumented, the Vox V846 is his only named one) -> Dallas Arbiter Fuzz Face (germanium; his main fuzz, inferred for this take) -> 100 W Marshall stacks (groundguitar documents the JTM45/100 Super 100 with 4x12s; no exact record for this session). Kramer screened the amp and miked it with a U67 and/or a Beyer M160, with compression, EQ and desk reverb; the room 'just resonates'. Eighth take is the master. No delay or modulation on the studio take.
notes: Amp: amalgam's 1966 JTM45/100 Super 100 (the model groundguitar documents) as a full rig, edge of breakup, so the fuzz does the gain. Fuzz (always on): a germanium Fuzz Face with AC128 transistors, Fuzz 10 / Vol 6, with the Strat voicing in front of it (the fuzz hears a single coil). Its fizz is trimmed at the end (eq_3k5 -2, eq_8k -3: 'less fizz'), standing in for Kramer's ribbon/U67 mics. The wah is SW6 + EXP A (the DAW wah). SW8 BOOST = TS9 clean push (not on the record); SW9 = an eighth-note echo at 88 BPM (not on the record); EMT 140 plate for the desk reverb. SW7 VIBE = the Uni-Vibe Hendrix played this song with live from 1969 (Woodstock): not on the 1968 take. Can't match: the stereo panning of the overdubs. The record is a half step down (tag eb). Opt-in record pitch: tone.csv pitch_st -1 (this row, or the @eb row for every Eb song; adds 11-31 ms latency), or tune the guitar down. Levelled offline with rigsim --exact to -14 LUFS (experiments D28).

left.label: Ibanez TS9 clean push, D0 T6 L10 (lead boost, not on the record)
Germanium Fuzz Face, AC128 transistors, Vol 6 Fuzz 10 Bias 5 (Strat voicing in front)
Marshall JTM45/100 Super 100 (1966), Vol I 6, edge of breakup (full rig, G12H 4x12)
Eighth-note echo 341 ms at 88 BPM (not on the record)

vibe.note: Not on the 1968 studio take: Hendrix's live Uni-Vibe (1969-70, Woodstock, Band of Gypsys), slow and fully mixed
